extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, academics, practitioners, and educated public)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria and practical standards used in short book reviews and instrument notices within a scientific journal issue (e.g., assessing scientific books, methods texts, instruments, and brief notices). Focuses on clarity, accuracy, suitability for audience, and practical performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity of coloured plates
rubrics_metrics.description: Plates should be 'sufficiently faithful to nature to enable the novice to identify the fruits'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality colour illustrations that accurately represent the subject enable novices to identify species even if microscopic/dissection details are absent. Specific plates (e.g., spindle, hawthorn, sweet briar, oak) are commended as examples of desirable fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of botanical detail in illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrations should include the botanical details necessary for identification; some botanical details can only be shown after dissection and may be absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that plates may omit microscopic/dissection-level details, but they should still permit field identification; balance between visual fidelity and botanical minutiae should suit the intended readership (novice vs specialist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful revision and composition of text
rubrics_metrics.description: The text must be carefully revised; hurried composition produces ambiguous or faulty sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ambiguous constructions, incorrect punctuation reproduction, and other composition faults. Examples of problematic sentences are cited to illustrate the need for careful editing and revision before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in orthography and typography (capitalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of capitals must be consistent; inconsistent capitalization (e.g., specific names starting with capitals in headings but not in text) is indefensible in botanical nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply consistent typographic conventions throughout (especially for scientific names), adhering to disciplinary norms (generally lowercase for generic and specific epithets in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct and up-to-date scientific nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the correct botanical names (e.g., Cytisus scoparius rather than out-of-date Sarothamnus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt current taxonomic names and avoid archaic synonyms unless explicitly justified; errors in nomenclature indicate poor editorial care and mislead readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of lists and indices (spelling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of illustrations and indices must be free from typographical errors (e.g., 'Rubus' misspelt 'Robus', 'scoparius' as 'scaparius').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully proof lists and indices; typographical errors there undermine confidence in the whole work and hinder readers finding information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical organisation and chapter structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Species should be grouped into meaningful chapters (e.g., hedgerow plants, forest trees, moorland/meadow/stream plants), and notes should vary in length according to importance and interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organise material so readers can find and use information easily; allocate space proportionally to the estimated importance of species and topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The book should be appropriate for its intended readers (novices, students, holiday naturalists); illustrations and text must match the readers' needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether level of detail, presentation, and examples are accessible and useful for the target audience; recommend to those whose expectations match the book's level (e.g., 'recommended to novices and students').

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and completeness of methodological description
rubrics_metrics.description: In methods texts, procedures and indicators must be explained sufficiently (e.g., colour-changes using dimethyl-amido-azo-benzol, rationale of Topfer's method).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough experimental detail and rationale for practitioners to understand what the observable outcomes mean and to reproduce methods; lack of explanation is a defect needing correction in later editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical applicability and utility to practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: A methods book should 'aid the practitioner in his investigation' and include methods of practical value to clinicians and workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise techniques that have demonstrated usefulness in clinical or laboratory practice and present them with emphasis on how they inform diagnosis/treatment; aim to broaden application of scientific methods in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based selection of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should confine treatment to methods 'which they have found during twelve years' trial of practical value'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer methods that have been tested and found valuable in practice; explicitly state basis for choosing methods (experience, trials) rather than presenting an exhaustive list of untested techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency for target users' expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must be explicit enough for the intended users—some practitioners may need more detailed explanations to implement methods themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match level of exposition to readers: for hands-on practitioners include operational details; for overview audiences, summarise and point to detailed sources. Note where the text is 'hardly explicit enough' for implementers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and forcefulness in presenting speculative arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculative works should present ideas (e.g., relativity of space/time, analogies between scales) clearly and forcefully; arguments should be simple and reasonable to appeal to readers willing to accept probabilistic reasoning in areas lacking logical certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between logically certain and speculative claims; present assumptions and the chain of reasoning plainly so readers can judge plausibility even without empirical verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit statement of assumptions in speculative/theoretical work
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of speculative works must state their fundamental assumptions (e.g., universe infinite in 3-D space and eternal; law of gravitation holds throughout infinite space; luminiferous ether properties constant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make all key assumptions explicit so readers can assess the scope and limits of the arguments and how conclusions depend on those premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of point of view and interpretive framing
rubrics_metrics.description: A speculative or interpretive work's chief value may be the point of view it presents, valid for readers who accept its premises and interpretative choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the book offers a useful conceptual framing or viewpoint that stimulates thought, even if empirical verification is impossible; clarity of that framing is a merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument durability and compactness
rubrics_metrics.description: Meteorological and recording instruments should be 'durable and compact' and 'easily fixed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider construction quality, robustness for field or institutional use, ease of installation and maintenance when evaluating instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument automation and continuous recording features
rubrics_metrics.description: Recorders should register for a day, week, month or any period automatically, be self-setting, and allow records to be examined as desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic/self-setting operation that permits continuous recording and later inspection increases instrument utility; these features are desirable for routine monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument scale uniformity and correction-free operation
rubrics_metrics.description: The scale should be 'uniform all through the year' and 'no correction is needed for the equation of time'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer instruments/calendars whose scales or record-keeping do not require seasonal or periodic user corrections, reducing user workload and error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and permanence of recorded output
rubrics_metrics.description: Records should be 'sharp and distinct, being black on white' and charts inexpensive ('only a few shillings a year').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate instruments on the legibility and permanence of their outputs and on the ongoing cost of consumables (charts/paper), since these affect long-term usability and operating cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance metrics for technical apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical devices (e.g., Dr. Gaede's high-vacuum pump) are assessed by measurable performance: guaranteed vacuum (0.00004 mm), evacuation time (2½ minutes for a Röntgen tube), attainment of the 'highest rarefaction yet reached'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspectors and buyers should look for quantified performance claims (vacuum level, speed, sensitivity); these should be backed by demonstrated or certified measures and references to prior reports where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational effectiveness (stability) in applied devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Devices such as gyroscopes are judged by their effectiveness in operation (e.g., 'kept upright although the centre of gravity is far above the point of suspension').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how well a device accomplishes its functional purpose under realistic operating conditions; demonstrations or specific use-cases help validate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and suitability of scientific equipment packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscopes and instrument sets should be complete (stand, coarse and micrometer fine adjustment, triple nosepiece, sub-stage condenser) and tailored for classes of work (from simple practical to critical research); price ranges reflect quality and configuration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether supplied components meet the intended applications (teaching, clinical, research), check availability of detailed catalogues and certificates, and consider price-to-feature trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements for job applications and appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointments/applications must be made on official forms, returned by specified deadlines, accompanied by particulars (e.g., not more than three recent testimonials), stamped addressed envelope; canvassing is a disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow stated procedural rules exactly; failure to use official forms, meet deadlines, include required enclosures, or canvass may result in disqualification regardless of merit. These are explicit grounds and quality-control measures for selection.
